safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports no unwell contacts and no nausea or vomiting.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated captures no nausea/vomiting, but does not mention 'no unwell contacts,' which is part of the gold fact.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting “no unwell contacts” slightly reduces epidemiologic/contextual information (e.g., infectious exposure risk), but it is unlikely to change immediate clinical decision-making for this self-limited viral/flu-like presentation. The note still captures the more clinically actionable negative symptoms (no nausea/vomiting).

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document safety-net/return precautions for red-flag worsening (chest pain, increasing shortness of breath, persistent/high fevers) can contribute to delayed re-evaluation and delayed treatment of potentially serious conditions (e.g., pneumonia, pulmonary embolism, cardiac ischemia) if the patient deteriorates. This creates a meaningful risk to patient safety even if no harm occurs in many cases.
